scope: Rank-16 49-frame LoRA smoke with native allocator split protection
summary: The PyTorch-documented max_split_size_mb setting changed the fragmentation failure from a 200 MiB FSDP gather to a 76 MiB adapter output, but the shared rank still lacked 13 MiB at peak and no checkpoint completed.
evidence: The remote PyTorch 2.6 runtime accepted backend:native, expandable_segments:True, and max_split_size_mb:128.
The prior 200 MiB all-gather failure did not recur at the same point; the eventual failure requested 76 MiB with 63 MiB physically free.
No checkpoint was written and result.json records PARTIAL.
lessons: Allocator tuning was directionally effective but only 13 MiB separates this workload from completion, making it too brittle for a long formal run on shared GPUs.
Use a 33-frame first curriculum phase to create durable activation headroom without reducing rank or attention targets.
limitations: No optimizer step completed; allocator improvement alone is not training evidence.
next_actions: Run rank-16 attention LoRA with random 33-frame native-16fps windows and the same split-protected allocator.
